messages.author: 31713d8bfe31b7ef
messages.subject: Repeated measurements
parts:
Hi everyone, I have a question regarding repeated measurements. I digitized my data set twice and I would like to average the measurements from the two digitizing sessions in my final analysis since the repeatability is not optimal. Is there a function for that in geomorph or do you have hints on how to do that?

Regards,
Hildur

messages.author: aab55242ff4da6c6
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Repeated measurements
parts:
Hildur,

There are two ways (or more) to tackle this problem.  Both of these require a factor for identifying individuals, which I call “ind” in the examples below.

One is to use the coords.subset function in geomorph.  Here is an example with our mosquito data, which has 4 measurements per individual

data(mosquito)
ind.shape <- coords.subset(mosquito$wingshape, mosquito$ind) # subsets the coordinates based on the variable, ind
means <- lapply(ind.shape, mshape) # creates a list of mean shapes, using the mshape function in geomorph

# or 

means <- t(sapply(ind.shape, mshape)) # creates a matrix of vectorized mean shapes

The other is to use advanced.procD.lm

gdf <- geomorph.data.frame(wingshape = mosquito$wingshape, ind=mosquito$ind)
apdlm <- advanced.procD.lm(wingshape~ind, ~1, groups = ~ind, iter=1, data = gdf) # a test with 1 iteration - not interested in the test, just want the output
apdlm$LS.means # the needed output;  the same as t(sapply(ind.shape, mshape)) above

Cheers!
Mike
